*H.comment: The y range -3.1 to 3.2 doubles to -6.2 to 6.4; the x range stays

*W.comment: The x range -6.5 to 6.5 doubles to -13 to 13; the y range stays

/.comment: Solves the linear system: the matrix times the result gives [ 5 6 ]

<.comment: Units are compared after conversion: 1 m is longer than 50 cm

ADDTMOD.comment: The sum X^2+12*X+9 reduces modulo 7 to X^2-2*X+2

AMORT.comment: First 12 monthly payments of 200 on 10000 at 6% a year: principal, interest, balance

ARCHIVE.comment: Backs up HOME to port 0 under the name BK; PVARS then lists it

ASN.comment: Puts « 1 » on key 11 (row 1, column 1, unshifted); RCLKEYS shows it

ASR.comment: The top bit stays set as the other bits move down

A→H.comment: The five digits come back in reverse order

BAUD.comment: The baud rate is the first element of IOPAR

BESTFIT.comment: Data that triple at each step fit an exponential model best

BIN.comment: Hexadecimal FF is eight ones in binary

BINS.comment: Two bins of width 2 from 0: counts per bin, then counts below and above

C2P.comment: The cycles (1 3) and (2 4) give the images 3, 4, 1, 2

CASE.comment: The test for 1 fails, the test for 2 passes and pushes B

CEIL.comment: A negative number rounds up towards zero

CF.comment: Sets flag 3, clears it, then tests it: 0 means clear

CIRC.comment: The two permutations are inverses, so the result is the identity

CLKADJ.comment: Moves the clock forward by one second (8192 ticks)
Moves the clock back by 2.5 seconds

CLΣ.comment: The old data is gone: only the new point 7 remains

COLΣ.comment: Column 2 is the independent variable, column 1 the dependent one

COMB.comment: The number of five-card hands from a 52-card deck

CONST.comment: With flag 61 set the value has no units; g is standard gravity

C→PX.comment: The origin falls on pixel 65, 32 of the default plot window
(-6.5,3.2), the plot window's upper-left point, is pixel 0, 0

DARCY.comment: Zero roughness at Reynolds number 1000 gives 64 divided by 1000

DDAYS.comment: From 1 January to 15 July 1991, in MM.DDYYYY form

DEF.comment: Defines F(X)=X^2, then calls F with 3

DEFINE.comment: Defines the function F, then calls it with 3

DELALARM.comment: Index 0 deletes every alarm, so FINDALARM then finds none

DELAY.comment: The delay is the first element of PRTPAR

DELKEYS.comment: Removes the assignment on key 11 only; the one on key 12 stays

DIAGMAP.comment: Squares the eigenvalues of the matrix, 1 and 4

DIV2MOD.comment: Quotient X, remainder X+4, which is X+1 modulo 3
11 is 4 modulo 7, so 11 divided by 4 gives 1, remainder 0

DIVPC.comment: 1/(1-X) as a series up to X^4

DO.comment: Multiplies by 3 until the value is above 50: 3, 9, 27, 81

DOLIST.comment: Two lists, the count 2, and a program that multiplies each pair

DOSUBS.comment: Adds each pair of neighbouring elements
SWAP - subtracts the earlier element from the later one in each pair

DUPN.comment: The count 2 copies the top two objects, the 2 and the 3

EGVL.comment: A quarter-turn rotation matrix has the eigenvalues i and -i

ENDSUB.comment: Windows of one element give 3 windows, so ENDSUB is 3 every time

EPSX0.comment: 1E-15 is below EPS, so its term becomes 0

ERR0.comment: Traps 1/0, clears the error record, then ERRN gives #0

ERRN.comment: 305h, 773 in decimal, is the code of Infinite Result

EULER.comment: 13 is prime, so 12 numbers up to it are coprime to it

EXGET.comment: The 2nd object is +, so its subexpression is A+B

EXP.comment: e^i has real part cos 1 and imaginary part sin 1, in radians

EXPANDMOD.comment: Modulo 7 the X term vanishes and 12 becomes -2

EXPM.comment: The final 5 is the x²/2 term, a digit EXP(x)-1 would round away

EXSUB.comment: Replaces the + subexpression, A+B, with E^F

FACTORS.comment: Each factor is followed by its multiplicity: 5, 3 squared, 2 cubed

FANNING.comment: Zero roughness at Reynolds number 1000 gives 16 divided by 1000

FC?C.comment: Flag 5 is set, so 0 comes back, and then flag 5 is cleared

FCOEF.comment: Root 1 twice (multiplicity 2) and a pole at 3 (multiplicity -1)

FFT.comment: A single 1 followed by zeros gives a flat spectrum

FINDALARM.comment: The alarm, on 1 January 2030, falls due after 1 January 2029
The alarm is at 12:00, before 13:00, so none is found
0 looks for a past-due alarm, and none is due

FIX.comment: Zero decimal places rounds 12.7 up and keeps the point

FOR.comment: Adds k from 1 to 5 to the 0 already on the stack
Counts from 1 to 10 in steps of 3

FS?C.comment: Returns 1 because flag 5 is set, then clears it, so FS? gives 0

GETI.comment: The list, the next position 2, and the element at position 1
After position 3 the index wraps round to 1

GOR.comment: ORs a 4 by 4 graphic into an 8 by 8 one at pixel 0, 0; the size is unchanged

GRAD.comment: 100 grads is a quarter circle, so its sine is 1

GROB.comment: 8 pixels wide and 2 high: FF is the first row, 00 the second

HMS+.comment: 0h59m59s plus 1 second carries over to exactly 1 hour

HORNER.comment: Divides by (X-3): the quotient, the point 3, and the value at 3
Divides by (X+1): the quotient, the point -1, and the value at -1

H→S.comment: Each character is two digits in reverse order: 41 is A, 42 is B

ICHINREM.comment: x is 2 modulo 3 and 1 modulo 5, giving -4 modulo 15

IFERR.comment: 1/0 fails, so the THEN part runs and pushes the text; the 1 and 0 stay

IFT.comment: The test 1 is not zero, so the program runs: 2 plus 3

INDEP.comment: A list also sets the range of the variable: T from 0 to 5

INT.comment: Integrates X^2 in X, evaluated at Y

ISPRIME?.comment: 91 is 7 times 13, so it is not prime

LASTARG.comment: The one argument, 16, comes back after the square root

LCXM.comment: Entry (i,j) is i plus j, for 2 rows and 3 columns

LDEC.comment: The right-hand side is 0 and the characteristic polynomial is X^2+1

LININ.comment: SIN(Y) does not contain X, so the term is linear

LSQ.comment: The vector is B, the matrix is A: three equations, two unknowns

LVAR.comment: SIN(X) is listed as a whole, not as X

MKISOM.comment: A rotation by π/2; the sign 1 marks a direct isometry

MOD.comment: The result takes the sign of the divisor, so -17 mod 5 is 3

NOT.comment: Every one of the 64 bits is inverted
The word size is 8, so only 8 bits are inverted

NSUB.comment: NSUB is 1, 2, 3 in turn, so each element is multiplied by its position

OBGET.comment: Counting A, +, B, * and C from the left, the 2nd is +
Counting A, * and B from the left, the 3rd is B

OBSUB.comment: Replaces the 3rd object, B, with C
